themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 203 THIS WEEK, a 268% increase from the 55.1-weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.28), coinciding with damaged tree complaints jumping 392% last week (56 vs. 11.4 avg) and overgrown tree/branches up 256% (16 vs. 4.5 avg)—indicating widespread pavement, vegetation, and sidewalk deterioration affecting neighborhood walkability and safety.
evidence: 203 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 55.1 weekly average (z-score: 6.28, 268% spike)
56 damaged tree complaints last week vs. 11.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.8, 392% spike)
16 overgrown tree/branch complaints last week vs. 4.5 weekly average (z-score: 5.58, 256% spike)
Community Board has repeatedly requested street reconstruction funding from DOT (recurring annual request)
reporting_angles: Ground-truth reporting: photograph worst affected streets and interview residents experiencing trip hazards, vehicle damage from potholes, or pedestrian safety concerns
City response investigation: why has street maintenance failed to prevent this concentration of complaints this week? Are crews deployed? What is DOT's repair timeline?

themes_detail.label: Mysterious Dead Animal Surge
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints surged to 15 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 314% spike from the 3.6-weekly baseline (z-score: 6.58), the largest percentage increase in the dataset—suggesting a possible public health or environmental event (wildlife disease, poisoning, or disposal crisis) requiring urgent investigation.
evidence: 15 dead animal complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.6 weekly average (z-score: 6.58, 314% spike—highest percentage increase in dataset)
Spike is temporally isolated; no follow-up spike data this week suggests event may have peaked or resolved
No Reddit or local news coverage of incident, indicating potential reporting gap
reporting_angles: Health department outreach: were there reports of disease, pest infestation, or intentional poisoning? Any public health alerts issued?
Neighborhood canvassing: interview residents about what they observed two weeks ago—timing, locations, patterns—to reconstruct the event

themes_detail.label: Street-Level Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 14 THIS WEEK, a 273% increase from the 3.8-weekly average (z-score: 6.25), with no corresponding increase in residential noise complaints, suggesting a localized construction, traffic, or event-related disturbance requiring source identification.
evidence: 14 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.8 weekly average (z-score: 6.25, 273% spike)
Residential noise complaints remain at baseline (668 total over 90 days, no acute spike noted), indicating source is external/commercial rather than neighbor-to-neighbor
Spike is concurrent with street condition crisis, suggesting possible construction or infrastructure work
reporting_angles: DOT/construction audit: is there permitted street work, utility repair, or demolition activity underway? Cross-reference 650 recent DOB permits (17 demolitions filed) against noise complaint locations
Community impact: which blocks are experiencing noise this week? Interview affected residents about timing and source of disturbance

themes_detail.label: Sewer System Degradation
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints increased 66% last week to 35 complaints vs. 21.1 weekly average (z-score: 5.3), sustained above baseline and converging with the broader infrastructure spike (street condition, tree damage), suggesting aging pipe or drainage system failure requiring engineering assessment.
evidence: 35 sewer complaints last week vs. 21.1 weekly average (z-score: 5.3, 66% spike)
Sewer complaints are part of broader infrastructure failure cluster: street condition (268% up), tree damage (392% up), obstruction (146% up) all spiking simultaneously last 1-2 weeks
Water system complaints remain elevated at 871 total over 90 days, indicating chronic water/drainage infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: DEP infrastructure assessment: request data on sewer pipe age, break rates, and maintenance schedules in Queens Village/Cambria Heights; are pipes pre-1970s infrastructure?
Resident impact stories: interview homeowners dealing with backed-up sewers or flooded basements; connect to broader neighborhood infrastructure neglect narrative

themes_detail.label: Interior Housing Defects Spike
themes_detail.summary: Flooring/stairs complaints jumped to 7 last week, a 300% increase from the 1.8-weekly average (z-score: 4.38), indicating possible widespread building code violations or structural settling affecting multiple residential units.
evidence: 7 flooring/stairs complaints last week vs. 1.8 weekly average (z-score: 4.38, 300% spike)
456 alteration permits filed in past 90 days; unclear if any are illegal work or deferred maintenance remediations
Community Board has repeatedly requested code enforcement expansion, suggesting chronic enforcement gap may be enabling housing violations
reporting_angles: DOB enforcement audit: pull complaint details from last week's 7 flooring/stairs complaints to identify if they cluster in one building or neighborhood block; assess whether violations are being remediated or ignored
Renter vulnerability story: interview affected tenants about housing quality and landlord responsiveness; connect to broader code enforcement gap identified in CB budget requests
